SOCKS5 accepted the request, but the public test site TLS response never arrived through the VPN. SOCKS CONNECT alone does not prove VLESS/REALITY or WireGuard connectivity. Check the server and the actual route.
The TLS handshake to a public HTTPS test site failed through the selected VPN. This is not necessarily the VPN server REALITY handshake; inspect the safe diagnostic stage and the egress route.
The public HTTPS connection closed before the TLS handshake finished. SOCKS5 is running, but the VPN server may still be unreachable or resetting traffic.

The Android native core exited during startup. The code below shows the last stage before the crash. This may be an app or engine compatibility issue, not the server. Share the stage code without configs or keys.

For Xray Preview: import VLESS/REALITY, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks or a WireGuard .conf, select a server, then tap Connect. The HTTPS check uses the local SOCKS listener before the VPN tunnel opens. REMOTE_TLS refers to the public HTTPS test host, not necessarily the REALITY server. LIC-Auto ranks working encrypted HTTPS connections at startup without background polling. LIC-Bay uses SOCKS5 CONNECT and UDP ASSOCIATE through ByeDPI with no direct fallback. Check HTTPS, DNS, IPv4/IPv6 and leaks before trusting this preview.
